verdict_text: YES. The script casts exactly the 112 projection matrices matched by full-match regex to bfloat16, leaves every other tensor float32 with unchanged values, deletes nothing (the buffer regex can never match), preserves names, enforces all four required checks before writing, and writes a sharded safetensors checkpoint under `out/T3` with the 256 MiB limit passed to the sharding helper. The only part not visible here is the `save_sharded_safetensors` helper, which is assumed to honour the byte limit and emit `model.safetensors.index.json`.
